main_text.p: sentia, nisi sit error, explicandum est, in desiderio, scilicet Domini. Sed hæc levia : versu 29. ad finem ותרוב [?] ultima litera debet esse Resch non Bet, רור [?] enim habitare significat, versu 30. בארין [?] post eos, loco Aleph reponendum ית [?] versi, 31. לי אלהך [?] Domino Deo tuo, pro לי [?] scribendum לרהוה [?] eodem versu רס בא [?] delendum punctum, quo in duas dictiones fit separatio & continuo legendum רסבא [?] qve[illegible, ~3 letters]dit ; eodem versu יקרון [?] delendum punctum ne fiant duæ voces, combusserunt ; comparatione textus Hebræo-Samaritani facile fuit ista corrige-re, sed de quo loco ista eruta essent, nescienti negotium facessere potuerunt, voces insolentes Syris & Chaldæis istæ videntur צריוח [?], qua significatur צרים [?] gentes רער [?] quæ pro Hebræo נקש [?] ista-queare מלמס [?] creavit, quæ vox est secunda Pentateuchi ; quæ dixi de superstitione Judaica circa nomen Tetragrammaton, quam ex v. 16. c. 3. page.notes: Page number: the left digit is damaged, read as 5 with [?]. A dark blot covers part of line 11 ("qve" to "dit"), so the covered letters are marked illegible. Hebrew words were copied as printed; several are uncertain and marked [?], especially those with vowel points or damaged letters (ותרוב, רור, ית, רער, נקש, מלמס, צריוח, צרים). The word "צרים" is partly covered by a printed box shape in the scan. The word at the line end "tan-" continues on the next page as "tancum", and the catchword "cum" is printed at the foot.
